# Ring Mint

> Ring Mint is a custom engagement ring concierge (a jewelry concierge, or jewellery concierge in British English). Rings are designed from scratch in CAD and manufactured to order, with natural or lab created diamonds sourced from a global network of more than two million stones. There is no showroom and no held inventory.

Founded by Chloe Alpert with the support of her family's jewelry business, Teaman Jewelry, in business since 1979. Beyond engagement rings, Ring Mint makes wedding and anniversary bands, necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and heirloom redesigns, at every price point, in lab created and natural diamonds, colored gemstones, and rare high-end stones. Serves clients across the United States and internationally. Contact: chloe@ringmint.com or WhatsApp +1 814 876 0095.

Elsewhere: [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/theringmint) · [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/ringmint) · [Pinterest](https://www.pinterest.com/theringmint) · [Trustpilot](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/ringmint.com)

## What makes the model different

Traditional jewelers buy stones and finished rings before knowing who wants them, and pay for retail space and sales staff. Those costs are recovered in the price of what sells. Ring Mint sources stones after a client describes what they want and manufactures after the design is approved, so there is no inventory cost and no incentive to steer a client toward a particular stone.

## Process

Seven steps, roughly two weeks of manufacturing once a design is approved:

1. Client gets in touch by form, email, or WhatsApp.
2. Call with the ring concierge; unlimited questions by text or WhatsApp thereafter.
3. Budget, deadline, stone preferences, and proposal timing are set.
4. Ring is designed from scratch in CAD; stones are sourced against the brief.
5. CAD is refined; an optional wax model is mailed for an at-home try-on.
6. Final design approved; ring manufactured to order in about two weeks.
7. Delivery with independent appraisal, final photographs, and fully insured shipping.

- [Three custom lab-grown diamond necklaces for wedding gifts, around $900 each](https://ringmint.com/blog/lab-grown-diamond-necklace-wedding-gifts/): A real commission for three 6mm lab-grown diamond wedding gift necklaces in 14k gold, around $900 each, with CAD and Pennsylvania studio photographs.
- [Ring Mint and Ring Concierge: two different companies, two different models.](https://ringmint.com/blog/ring-mint-vs-ring-concierge/): Ring Mint and Ring Concierge are unrelated companies with similar names. Ring Concierge was founded in 2013 by Nicole Wegman, is based in New York, and operates fine jewelry stores in Soho and on Madison Avenue in New York, at Westfield Century City in Los Angeles, and at Town Center in Boca Raton, plus a Midtown Manhattan bridal showroom by appointment; it sells ready-to-wear fine jewelry alongside bridal and an online ring builder. Ring Mint was founded in 2025 by Chloe Alpert, a second-generation jeweler in Pennsylvania, has no store, showroom, employees or inventory, and designs every piece from scratch to order. Ring Concierge suits buyers who want to try rings on in a store; Ring Mint suits buyers who want a ring designed from scratch without retail overhead in the price.
- [Toi et moi engagement rings: how to design one that actually works.](https://ringmint.com/blog/toi-et-moi-engagement-rings/): A toi et moi engagement ring sets two centre stones side by side on a single band; the name is French for "you and me". Designing one well comes down to four decisions: whether the stones match or contrast, their size ratio (equal, or roughly 60:40 for a deliberate asymmetry), their orientation on the finger, and matching their table heights so light hits both at once. A toi et moi will not sit flush against a straight wedding band because its widest point is off-centre, so the band must be contoured, which effectively requires custom work.
- [What a $5,000 engagement ring actually gets you in 2026.](https://ringmint.com/blog/5000-dollar-engagement-ring/): At retail in September 2026, a $5,000 budget buys roughly a 2 to 3 carat lab grown diamond plus a quality setting, or a natural diamond of about 1 to 1.3 carats with a simpler setting. Checked prices at Brilliant Earth included a 1.23 ct lab round D VVS1 at $1,030 and a 3.04 ct lab oval F VS2 at $3,260, while Blue Nile listed 1.00 ct natural rounds around $2,110 to $2,239. Lab diamond pricing is not linear with carat weight, so a larger stone can cost less than a smaller one. Ring Mint clients typically pay 30 to 50 percent less than comparable retail prices because there is no store or inventory.
- [Lab diamond vs. moissanite: the honest comparison.](https://ringmint.com/blog/lab-diamond-vs-moissanite/): A lab grown diamond is a diamond: carbon in a cubic crystal structure, hardness 10 on the Mohs scale. Moissanite is silicon carbide, a different mineral entirely, hardness about 9.25, doubly refractive, and with roughly 2.4 times the dispersion of diamond, which produces noticeably more rainbow fire. Moissanite's main historical advantage was price, and the collapse in lab grown diamond prices since 2020 has narrowed that gap substantially. Moissanite is a legitimate choice when disclosed; the problem is sellers passing it off as lab grown diamond.
- [IGI vs. GIA for lab grown diamonds: what changed, and which report to get.](https://ringmint.com/blog/igi-vs-gia-lab-grown/): As of late 2025 GIA no longer applies 4Cs colour and clarity grades to laboratory-grown diamonds. It issues a Laboratory-Grown Diamond Quality Assessment with a two-tier designation, Premium or Standard, and stones below the minimum threshold receive no designation at all. GIA's stated reason is that more than 95 percent of lab grown diamonds fall into a very narrow range of colour and clarity. IGI continues to grade lab diamonds on the full 4Cs, which makes IGI the practical choice for a buyer who wants a specific colour and clarity grade. GIA remains the standard for natural diamonds.
- [Holiday proposal order-by dates for a custom ring.](https://ringmint.com/blog/holiday-proposal-ring-deadlines/): Order-by dates to start a custom engagement ring for the 2026 to 2027 proposal season, worked backwards from each occasion. Thanksgiving November 26 2026, start by October 8 (comfortable) or November 5 (last call). Christmas Day December 25 2026, start by November 6 or December 4 at the latest. New Year's Eve December 31 2026, start by November 12 or December 10. Valentine's Day February 14 2027, start by December 27 or January 24. Custom rings take three to six weeks and the trade runs longer queues from mid-November.
- [How long does a custom engagement ring take?](https://ringmint.com/blog/how-long-custom-engagement-ring-takes/): A custom engagement ring takes about three to six weeks from first conversation to delivery. Manufacturing is roughly two weeks and is the most predictable stage. The variable is the design phase, which runs from a few days to several weeks depending on how quickly the client decides. Sourcing an unusual or rare stone, an optional mailed wax model, and hand engraving each add time. Ring Mint builds the schedule backwards from a proposal date.
- [What a wax model try-on is, and why every custom ring should have one.](https://ringmint.com/blog/wax-model-ring-try-on/): A wax model is a castable wax replica of a specific custom ring, cut from the same CAD file that will later be cast in metal, and mailed to the client on request to try on before production begins. It answers scale and fit questions that a CAD render cannot. Most of the time it confirms the design is right; when it does prompt a change, clients usually go smaller on the center stone rather than larger. It is real wax and it is fragile, so it is meant for a brief try-on rather than for wearing. The client keeps it; a fresh wax is cut for the actual casting. It cannot show metal color, sparkle, or weight. Ring Mint mails one on request and it adds roughly a week to the schedule.
- [Custom vs. customizable: why a ring builder is not a custom ring.](https://ringmint.com/blog/custom-vs-customizable-ring/): A ring builder pairs a stone with a setting that already exists in a fixed catalog; fully custom means the setting is modeled from scratch in CAD for one client, so there is no mold and no catalog constraint. Semi-custom sits between the two. Custom is usually not more expensive, because the design work is a small share of a ring's cost next to the stone and the metal.
- [Are the diamonds in TikTok live auctions real?](https://ringmint.com/blog/are-tiktok-diamonds-real/): Yes, almost always real lab grown diamonds at $100 to $200 per carat, occasionally moissanite; the risk is quality (strong fluorescence, poor cuts, low clarity), which a 10 to 30 second bidding window can't reveal.
- [Blowing the whistle on fake lab diamonds on eBay](https://ringmint.com/blog/ebay-lab-diamonds-moissanite/): Ring Mint bought 50+ stones listed as lab grown diamonds from 20+ eBay sellers; every one was moissanite (silicon carbide), most colored ones were white moissanite with a pavilion coating that polishes off and is damaged by solvents like nail polish remover, the stones are cut with the optic axis through the table so facet doubling is hidden and thermal pen testers pass them, and they are worth under $100 each. File an eBay "item not as described" claim within 30 days.
- [About Chloe Alpert](https://ringmint.com/about/): Founder biography and credentials: second-generation jeweler, in the trade since 2009, Cert GA from Gem-A London, daughter of Teaman Jewelry founder Sharon. Author of every page on the site.
- [Reviews](https://ringmint.com/reviews/): Every client review in full with links to the verified originals on Trustpilot; rated 5.0 out of 5 from 6 reviews as of September 2026, clients in the US, UK, Estonia and Monaco.
- [Contact](https://ringmint.com/contact/): Email chloe@ringmint.com, WhatsApp +1 814 876 0095, or a short form. Replies within one business day. No concierge fee.

## Pricing

- Ring Mint clients typically pay 30 to 50% less than the price of a comparable ring at a jewelry store or large online retailer, because there is no store, no showroom, no sales staff, no held inventory, and no separate concierge fee. Clients pay for the stone and the ring.
- Ring Mint does not publish a price list. Price guides on this site quote dated public retail prices from large online retailers as the benchmark, then apply that 30 to 50% difference.
- There is no minimum budget. Last updated September 2026.

## Key facts

- Lab created diamonds are chemically and physically identical to mined diamonds: same carbon, same cubic crystal structure, same hardness of 10 on the Mohs scale. They cannot be distinguished by eye or with a loupe.
- Lab created diamonds cost a fraction of comparable natural stones, but their resale value is poor and falling. Natural diamonds also resell well below retail price. Neither is an investment.
- Diamonds are graded by IGI or GIA on the standard 4Cs scale regardless of origin.
- Every Ring Mint ring is delivered with an independent appraisal and the stone's grading report.
- There is no separate concierge fee. Clients pay for the stone and the ring.

## Payment and returns

- Payment is split in two: a 50% deposit on the center stone, and a 50% deposit on production of the final ring. The remaining balance is due after the finished ring is reviewed, before it ships.
- Diamonds and deposits are refundable for up to 20 days, or until production begins on the final ring, whichever comes first.
- Custom rings are not returnable once production has started, because they are made to the client's specification. Ring Mint will re-work or refine a piece, or liquidate it and apply credit as close to cost as possible.
- Ring Mint guarantees its work against defects and manufacturing problems.
- All shipping is fully insured.
